questions.q: Do you prefer tea or coffee?
questions.answer: Tea, without a doubt. It's a bit of a [[ritual]] here, and I probably have three or four cups a day. Coffee is fine occasionally, but nothing quite beats a hot cup of tea in the morning.

questions.q: How do you take your tea?
questions.answer: I like it strong, with milk and just a little sugar. My mother sometimes adds ginger or cardamom, especially in winter, which gives it a lovely [[aromatic]] quality. Plain black tea is fine too, but milk tea is my favourite.

questions.q: Do you often drink tea outside the home?
questions.answer: Quite often, yes. Roadside tea stalls are everywhere here, and meeting friends at one is a big part of our social life. There's a [[convivial]] atmosphere at those stalls that you simply can't find in a café.

questions.q: Is coffee becoming more popular in your country?
questions.answer: Definitely, especially among young people in cities. New coffee shops keep opening in Dhaka, and they've become [[trendy]] places to study or meet friends. Tea is still far more common, though, particularly outside the big cities.

questions.q: Do you think you drink too much tea?
questions.answer: Possibly, yes. Three or four cups a day may be a bit much, especially in the evening, as it sometimes keeps me awake. I've been trying to [[cut back]] after dinner, though with mixed results so far.
